jobs.occupation: PhD Research Fellow in AI Native Networking for Healthcare
jobs.description:
We seek a PhD Research Fellow for a 3-year position in the SYNAPSE project. The successful candidate will have a solid background in computer networking and an interest in developing machine-learning methods for network control and network-aware distributed learning.

Section for Medical Information and Communication Technology (Medical ICT Research), The Intervention Centre (see: http://www.ivs.no), at Oslo University Hospital offers a full-time PhD Fellowship. The recruited PhD Fellow will be part of the Wireless Sensor Network Research Group of Professor Ilangko Balasingham and will be enrolled in the PhD program at the University of Oslo

We seek candidates with a solid background in computer networking who want to develop machine-learning methods for network control and network-aware distributed learning.

Oslo University Hospital is a workplace with great diversity. We believe this is crucial for solving our tasks in the best possible way. We want this diversity to be reflected among the applicants for our positions, and we encourage all qualified candidates, regardless of background, to apply!

Arbeidsoppgaver
About SYNAPSE

SYNAPSE, funded by the Research Council of Norway, develops networks that adapt their decisions to network conditions and the clinical urgency of the information they carry. Learning is integrated into network control to support decisions about scheduling, routing and resource allocation. For example, an urgent clinical alert should reach its destination promptly even when links are congested and patients are moving.

The project also develops distributed and federated learning methods that adapt to connectivity, available resources and clinical priorities. Network control and distributed learning are designed together, so that the network supports learning and learning remains effective when communication is constrained. The methods are evaluated in remote patient monitoring and hospital-at-home scenarios.  

This position focuses on network protocols and their control at the MAC, network, transport and cross-layer levels, combined with machine learning. It does not cover hardware, antennas, circuits or physical-layer signal processing, and is not a general data-science position. Applicants must document relevant computer-networking knowledge and experience.

Research areas

• Learning-based network control, including scheduling, link selection, routing and resource allocation in wireless and edge networks.
• Reinforcement learning and multi-agent reinforcement learning for distributed network decision-making.
• Graph and hypergraph representation learning of network state, including temporal graph neural networks.
• Network- and urgency-aware distributed and federated learning, adapting the exchange of data and model updates to network conditions and clinical priorities.
• Evaluation through network simulation and emulation, and with real remote patient monitoring data.
Responsibilities

• Develop and evaluate learning-based methods for urgency-aware network control and network-aware distributed learning.
• Implement and test the methods using network simulation or emulation and real monitoring data.
• Publish in leading networking and machine-learning venues and complete a PhD at the University of Oslo, Faculty of Medicine.                Kvalifikasjoner (overskrift)
Required qualifications

• A master’s degree (120 ECTS), including a thesis, in computer science, network or communication engineering, electrical engineering or equivalent.
• A relevant bachelor’s degree (180 ECTS), with a total of five years of higher education.
• A solid foundation in computer networking, demonstrated through relevant coursework and a substantial project, thesis or research experience involving network protocols, wireless or mobile networks, routing or network performance.
• Coursework or project experience in machine learning, and good programming skills in Python.
• A weighted average grade of B or better on the master’s degree, as required by the University of Oslo.
• A master’s thesis graded B or better (Norwegian grading scale or equivalent).          
Preferred qualifications

• Experience with reinforcement learning or graph neural networks.
• Experience with network simulation or emulation tools, such as ns-3, OMNeT++ or Mininet.
• Publications or a master’s thesis combining networking and machine learning.
Language Requirements Applicants who are not proficient in a Scandinavian language must document English proficiency through one of the following: TOEFL: at least 600 (paper-based) or 92 (internet-based); IELTS Academic: at least 6.5, with no section below 5.5; Cambridge CAE/CPE: grade A or B.  

Personal Qualities

• Ability to work independently and collaboratively.
• A structured, precise and adaptable working style.
• Strong communication and teamwork skills.
• A positive attitude and ability to manage a dynamic work environment.
• A high level of professionalism and work ethic.
We offer

• A fully funded, full-time three-year PhD position. Salary according to the Norwegian state salary scale (approximately NOK 550,800–587,000 per year).
• Supervision by Dr Roufaida Laidi (PI), Prof. Ilangko Balasingham and Dr Hemin Ali Qadir, in collaboration with Prof. Tarik Taleb (Ruhr University Bochum).
• A clinical research environment at The Intervention Centre, Oslo University Hospital.
• Access to high-performance computing infrastructure at OUS and national e-infrastructure services.
• An inclusive, interdisciplinary research environment at the Intervention Centre, OUS.
• Pension, insurance and welfare schemes through the Norwegian public sector.
• Family-friendly surroundings with cultural and outdoor opportunities in Oslo.            
Your application

• Submit a cover letter of at most one page explaining your interest in SYNAPSE and your fit with the position. 
Identify:

• Your computer-networking background, naming relevant coursework, a thesis, substantial projects or publications and explaining your own contribution.
• Your experience implementing machine-learning methods and using network simulation, emulation or testbeds.
• The research area or areas above that best match your background and interests.
Supporting documents 

• A CV.
• Transcripts for your bachelor’s and master’s degrees, with the grading scale or diploma supplement.
• Copies of your diplomas.
• Documented English proficiency.
• Names and contact details of two referees, at least one academic. Referees must not be family members.
• Documents not in English or a Scandinavian language must be accompanied by a certified translation. Applications without transcripts and diplomas will not be assessed.

jobs.description:
About the position
At the Centre for Precision Psychiatry, Institute of Clinical Medicine, University of Oslo, there is a full-time, 2,5 years position available as a Researcher in artificial intelligence (AI), statistical modelling, and computational method development.

We invite applications from highly motivated candidates with a strong background in mathematics, statistics, computer science, data science, artificial intelligence, machine learning, computational modelling, engineering, physics, bioinformatics, or a related quantitative discipline. The position is part of an international and interdisciplinary research environment at the forefront of AI-driven precision neuroscience and precision medicine. The position is part of a collaborative effort between the University of Oslo, Oslo University Hospital, UC San Diego, the J. Craig Venter Institute (JCVI), and affiliated partners. The successful candidate will contribute to the development, implementation, and application of computational and AI-based methods for integrating multimodal brain imaging, genomics, registry, clinical, and other biomedical data, with the aim of improving understanding, prediction, and risk stratification of dementia, Alzheimer’s disease, and related neuropsychiatric disorders.
 
The position is linked to the “ResiliDem” project and the “Talent Utland” programme, funded by the Research Council of Norway. This is a unique opportunity to work on next-generation AI and statistical modelling approaches for large-scale, longitudinal, and potentially federated datasets, bridging computational innovation, biology, and clinical applications.
More about the position
The Centre for Precision Psychiatry is dedicated to research on severe mental and neuropsychiatric disorders. The Centre runs multidisciplinary studies involving hospital departments in Oslo, research groups at the University of Oslo, and international collaborators. The main goal is to develop tools and knowledge for precision medicine in brain disorders, using advanced statistical methods and AI tools for the analysis of large-scale genetic, neuroimaging, registry, clinical, and molecular data.

The Centre has access to large datasets including biomarkers, clinical and cognitive variables, genotyping and sequencing data, and MRI brain imaging data. In addition, we work closely with national population cohorts such as Tromsø, HUSK, and HUNT, Nordic registry and biobank resources, and large international consortia including PGC, ENIGMA, ADNI, NBDC, UK Biobank and others. We also collaborate with international partners at UC San Diego and the J. Craig Venter Institute, and with leading industry partners such as Nvidia, OpenAI, and Microsoft.

For more information about the Centre, please visit our website: Centre for Precision Psychiatry - Centre for Precision Psychiatry

The researcher hired for this position will work in a multidisciplinary team including clinicians, neuroscientists, geneticists, statisticians, applied mathematicians, AI researchers, and computer scientists. The candidate will contribute to computational method development, statistical modelling, machine learning, and AI-based analysis of large and complex biomedical datasets. The work will include development, implementation, testing, documentation, and application of reproducible analytical pipelines.

The candidate will work with the Centre’s datasets, analytical methodology, and computational tools, including state-of-the-art data storage and research infrastructure hosted at the USIT TSD service, with access to high-performance GPU computing resources for large-scale AI and deep-learning applications: Services for sensitive data (TSD) - University of Oslo

Our research environment is international, friendly, and inspiring, and the position represents a unique opportunity for career development for a motivated candidate with strong quantitative and computational skills.

• Perform data processing, quality control, harmonization, feature engineering, and model validation using large-scale datasets such as UK Biobank, NBDC, All of Us, HUNT, HUSK, and other Norwegian, Nordic, and international resources.
• Develop and maintain reproducible analytical pipelines in collaboration with researchers, postdoctoral fellows, and international partners, including collaborators at UC San Diego.
• Contribute to AI-based and potentially federated/online analytical frameworks for secure analysis across computational environments and research partners.
• Collaborate with clinicians, neuroscientists, geneticists, statisticians, and computer scientists to interpret findings and support applications in early diagnosis, prediction, and patient stratification.
• Contribute to scientific reports, presentations, manuscripts, documentation, and project deliverables. Qualifications

• Appointment to the position of Researcher in position code 1109 requires a university education equivalent to a PhD in one of the fields above or similar.
• Strong programming skills in Python, R, MATLAB, Julia, or similar programming languages, with emphasis on data analysis, statistical modelling, and AI/machine learning.

• Experience with handling, analysing, or modelling large and complex datasets.
• Experience with reproducible research practices, including documentation, structured analytical workflows, and version control.
• Excellent proficiency in written and spoken English.  
Preferred skills

• Experience with multimodal data integration, longitudinal or prediction modelling, foundation models, federated learning, or other advanced computational/AI approaches.
• Experience with human genetics, omics, brain imaging, registry, clinical, or other biomedical datasets, preferably related to neuroscience, Alzheimer’s disease, or precision medicine.

Your immediate leader will be the unit leader of Colourlab.
About the project
The CAPTURE project is an EU-funded Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Doctoral Network dedicated to advancing wireless capsule endoscopy (WCE) through developments in computer vision and artificial intelligence. The project aims to improve image-based diagnosis, monitoring, and treatment by developing methods that reduce clinicians’ workload, enhance imaging quality, and support more accurate and timely diagnoses.

CAPTURE combines research with a strong focus on doctoral training, preparing a new generation of researchers to work at the interface of technology and medicine. The consortium brings together expertise from academia, industry, and hospitals, ensuring that the research is both scientifically rigorous and clinically relevant.The project focuses on inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), reflecting its growing prevalence in Europe. As many of the methods developed have broader applicability, the project will also consider other gastrointestinal diseases. These goals will be achieved through the recruitment and training of 15 doctoral candidates in an international and intersectoral environment, providing interdisciplinary expertise across the technical, clinical, and applied aspects of WCE. 
Duties of the position
Automated approaches for pathology detection using WCE are generally based on recent AI models. These models often result in black-box decisions. For a clinician to use these systems, the basis for diagnostic decision should be clearly explained.

The PhD candidate will help develop explainable AI (XAI) methods for automated diagnostic decision systems to enhance the explainability and actionability of their predictions for doctors. The candidate will also evaluate the generated explanations with medical doctors to assess their relevance, usefulness, and importance in clinical settings.

• Complete the doctoral education until obtaining a doctorate
• Carry out research of good quality within the framework described above
• Academic publications and popular science dissemination
• Participate in the Colourlab research group

• Participate in international activities such as conferences and/or research stays at foreign educational institutions. Particularly, secondments of a few months’ duration are foreseen to Robert Gordon University, UK and Technical University of Darmstadt, Germany.

• Master students can apply, but the master's degree must be obtained and documented before starting the position.

If you do not have letter grades from previous studies, you must have an equally good academic foundation. If you have a weaker academic background, you may be considered if you can document that you are exceptionally suited for a PhD education, for example through relevant work experience and/or peer-reviewed academic works.

• Experience with computer vision, medical image processing, self-supervised learning or learning in low-data regimes.
• Experience with statistical signal processing and pattern recognition will be counted positive.
• Experience with pretrained representation models, transfer learning and xAI.

• Knowledge of explainable AI, uncertainty estimation, calibration, out-of-distribution detection, adversarial robustness, or causal analysis.

Emphasis will be placed on personal qualities.

About Integreat
See the video for more information about Integreat.
Video: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/-_I52cJHiW4About Integreat 
Integreat - Norwegian Centre for Knowledge-driven Machine Learning is a Centre of Excellence, funded by the Research Council of Norway (2023-33). Integreat has two branches, one in Oslo (University of Oslo, UiO) and one in Tromsø (UiT The Arctic University of Norway).

Machine learning is the mathematical and computational engine of Artificial Intelligence (AI), and therefore it is a fundamental force of technological progress in our increasingly digital, data- and algorithm-driven world. Integreat develops theories, methods, models, and algorithms that integrate general and domain-specific knowledge with data, laying the foundations of next generation machine learning. We do this by combining the mathematical and computational cultures, and the methodologies and theories, of statistics, logic, language technology, ethics and machine learning, in new and unique ways.

Focus of Integreat is to develop groundbreaking methods and theories, and therefore solving fundamental problems in science, technology, health and society. Integreat draws on the research strengths of researchers and students from the departments of Mathematics, Informatics, Philosophy, and the Oslo Centre for Biostatistics and Epidemiology at UiO, the Norwegian Computing Centre (NR) and the ML group at UiT, with members from the departments of Physics and Technology, Mathematics and Statistics, and Computer Science. 
Project description
Vision-language models (VLMs) can name what is in a picture, but they often miss what is happening in it. Shown a park scene, a model may list "a dog", "a Frisbee" and "a park" and still fail to say that the dog is leaping to catch the Frisbee mid-air. The same gap shows up when a model misreads a symbolic painting or gives a vague description of a medical image. More training data does not close this gap, because the models have no explicit representation of how the objects in a scene relate to each other.

This project gives VLMs that representation. You will develop panoptic scene graphs, in which every object and background region in an image becomes a node and the edges encode spatial, semantic and relational context. The graphs are built from superpixels rather than the fixed square patches used in standard vision transformers. Superpixels follow object boundaries, so the nodes of the graph are meaningful from the start. The project builds directly on our recent work on superpixel tokenization for vision transformers (ECCV Workshops 2024, NeurIPS 2025).

The scene graph is then fused with a large language model (LLM), and the two parts inform each other. The LLM guides which objects and relations the vision model should focus on, and the graph grounds the LLM's answers in what is actually in the image, which reduces hallucination. Because a scene graph has the same form as a knowledge graph, it also opens the way to graph-based visual retrieval-augmented generation (graph visual RAG), where a model links what it sees to external knowledge before it answers.

The aim is a new class of VLMs that reason over images instead of only describing them. Such models would be more accurate, more explainable (each answer can be traced to nodes and edges in the graph) and more useful where deep understanding matters. Examples include a robot that follows an instruction such as "place the red mug next to the laptop onto the top shelf", a medical system that reasons about the relations between structures in an X-ray, and a self-driving car that anticipates how pedestrians and vehicles will interact.

As a PhD fellow on the project, you will contribute to:

• develop superpixel-based panoptic segmentation models built on modern transformer architectures
• design methods that predict relations between segmented regions and generate panoptic scene graphs
• fuse scene graphs with LLMs for visual question answering and grounded reasoning, including graph visual RAG
• publish and present your results at leading machine learning and computer vision venues

We are building a self-hosted Kubernetes cluster that will serve as a multi-purpose platform for internal web services, CI runners, remote devcontainers, and hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) environments. This is not about maintaining an existing setup. It is about designing and implementing the foundation from scratch. 

Your mission follows this: to design, implement, and operationalize a highly available and scalable Kubernetes cluster that is adopted by developers and actively serving at least one of its intended purposes within the first six months. 

You will be part of Team Factory, which builds the internal infrastructure and tooling that engineering depends on. This is a role with real ownership, where there is room to become the key Kubernetes contributor in the company. 

What You Will Do
• 
Design and implement a highly available, self-hosted Kubernetes cluster

• 
Own cluster architecture, scalability, and lifecycle management

• 
Build a multi-purpose cluster supporting staging, production, CI runners, and remote dev containers.

• 
Develop internal tooling in Python and contribute to Kubernetes-specific components in Go where relevant

• 
Design resource-aware workload orchestration with priority- and capability-aware queueing mechanisms.

• 
Expose and integrate Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) setups into the platform

What we are looking for
We are looking for a Senior Engineer who understands Kubernetes beyond surface-level usage. You are comfortable operating between application developers and bare-metal infrastructure, and you proactively propose solutions rather than waiting for direction. 

You are motivated by ownership. You want to design something properly, build it, and maintain it over time. You thrive in environments where responsibility is real, and the technical bar is high. You think about how your technical decisions translate into value for real end users, and you are motivated by being part of building something that operates reliably in critical, real-world contexts where performance, correctness, and usability truly matter.

We believe the right candidate brings:
• 
5+ years of relevant experience in platform, infrastructure, or backend engineering

• 
Strong Kubernetes experience as a power user and at cluster-architecture level, not only deploying workloads

• 
Experience designing and operating self-hosted or on-prem Kubernetes environments

• 
Solid software engineering background and mindset, with comfort in languages like Python (for internal tooling) and Go

• 
Strong Linux fundamentals

• 
Experience with Docker and GitHub Actions

• 
Highly efficient and structured technical communication skills, expressing decisions and trade-offs in a clear manner

• 
Fluent in English (Norwegian not required)

Nice-to-haves:
• 
Experience with GitHub Actions Runner Controller (ARC)

• 
Dynamic VLAN configuration

• 
OpenStack

• 
Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) environments

• 
Building internal developer platforms

• 
Bare-metal-as-a-service concepts

• 
On-prem infrastructure management

Why You Should Join
At Six Robotics, we're not just building software - we're redefining how unmanned systems operate in the real world. If you're driven by meaningful problems, technical depth, and the chance to shape something from the ground up, you'll find your place here.

• 
Work on problems that matter

Our technology helps unlock smarter, safer, and more adaptable UAV operations in defense and industry, solving real challenges with direct, tangible impact.

• 
Lead the shift in a hardware-dominated space

We're bringing modern AI, autonomy, and scalable software into a field that's long relied on rigid, pre-programmed systems, to change how UAVs are designed, deployed, and managed.

• 
Build from zero, shape the future

Join early and help define the core systems, tools, and culture of a company that’s still being built - where your ideas, code, and decisions will have a lasting influence.

• 
Work with purpose, supported by great benefits You'll be part of a mission-driven team that values clarity, integrity, and collaboration, offering competitive pay, equity potential, strong insurance and pension plans, and ongoing learning opportunities.

Our Recruitment Process
• 
Screening interview with one of our recruiters to get to know you better (30 min).

• 
Meet & Greet with someone from the team to learn more about us (60 min).

• 
Programming assignment to be solved in your own time, followed by a technical interview more closely related to the specifics of the role (90 min).

• 
Final interview with our CTO and Head of People (45 min)

Reference check followed by an offer if everything goes well. We consider applications continuously, so don’t hold off with applying if this looks interesting. 

Our Commitment to Inclusion 

At Six Robotics, we are committed to creating a workplace built on respect, integrity, and collaboration. We value different perspectives and experiences, and we believe that diversity within our team strengthens both our work and our culture. We encourage all qualified candidates to apply and help us build technology that makes a real impact.

All employees at Six Robotics are required to undergo a security clearance due to our close collaboration with the Norwegian Armed Forces. While prior clearance is not necessary, the clearance process will be initiated as part of onboarding.
